topic: Simmis: Self-Hosted Shared Memory Workspace for People and AI Agents

key_points: Primary source: self-hosted workspace where people and AI agents share one memory — chat rooms, wiki, knowledge bases, an accounting book, and a code repository, all versioned and queryable on one substrate.
Reference application for the replikativ stack (Datahike, konserve, yggdrasil, kabel, kontor, spindel, dvergr).
Clojure, MIT license, created 2026-08-20, ~5 stars / 2 forks. Status: early 'release early' first public cut, used daily but with rough edges.
Rooms = conversation with durable memory; humans and agents are the same kind of participant (a 'party'), so @mention works across both; rooms can mirror to Telegram.
Knowledge bases = own Datahike DB holding wiki pages, blocks, links, typed entities; [[Title]] links stored as datoms so backlinks/neighborhood queries are ordinary queries.
Proposals = every governed agent write lands on a fork (yggdrasil branch), shows semantic diff, merges only with :merge authority — control that lets you be generous with what agents may write.
Time travel: stores keep history, any KB readable as-of a point in time.
The book: governed double-entry ledger (kontor); unbalanced entries rejected in the writer so an agent cannot corrupt the ledger.
Agents run in an SCI sandbox with curated vocabulary (wiki/, kb/, kontor/, proposal/, workflow/, muschel shell, datahike.api); can schedule recurring workflows.
Intake: web-clipper browser extension, mail accounts, screen capture, voice notes all land in the same substrate.
Client runs a real Datahike replica in the browser (IndexedDB-backed), kept in sync by konserve-sync; queries are local, server is the authorization boundary, not a query API.
Quick start: JDK 21+, Node 18+, npm install, clj -M:dev; UI at localhost:8080, ws at 47295.
LLM providers via env keys (FIREWORKS/OPENAI/ANTHROPIC/GROQ); fallback model accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p2; per-room model settings.

Known gaps: no integration-level auth test; blob reads authenticated but not authorized; agent sandbox is a soft boundary (not a VM); no migration tooling; must set SIMMIS_JWT_SECRET in prod; room apps private; single-node only.
Universal memory layer for AI agents (~63.8k stars) — the dominant incumbent in the agent-memory space.
Positioned as a drop-in memory layer/API rather than a full self-hosted workspace; focuses on memory extraction, storage, and retrieval for agents.
Contrast: Simmis is a whole self-hosted workspace (chat+wiki+ledger+repo) on one substrate, not just a memory layer.
Platform for stateful agents with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time (~24.3k stars).
Emphasizes agent memory and self-improvement; Simmis differentiates on shared human+agent memory with fork-and-review governance and a real ledger.
Open-source AI memory platform for agents; self-hosted knowledge-graph engine for persistent long-term memory across sessions (~30.1k stars).
Knowledge-graph-centric memory; Simmis uses Datalog/Datahike with time travel and proposals rather than a graph engine.
Zep: long-term memory for AI agents (~4.8k stars); examples, integrations, and more.
Another memory-layer incumbent; reinforces that Simmis's differentiator is the full self-hosted workspace + governance model, not memory alone.

stats.fact: Simmis is the reference application for the replikativ stack and is built in Clojure/ClojureScript, licensed MIT.
Simmis was created 2026-08-20 and is an early 'release early' first public cut; ~5 stars / 2 forks at research time.
The client runs a real Datahike replica in the browser (IndexedDB-backed); queries are local and the server is the authorization boundary, not a query API.
Datahike, the underlying durable Datalog database, drew 146 points on Hacker News.
Incumbent agent-memory projects: mem0 ~63.8k stars, cognee ~30.1k, letta ~24.3k, zep ~4.8k, langmem ~1.6k.
Simmis agents run in an SCI sandbox with a curated vocabulary; the sandbox is explicitly a soft boundary, not a VM.
replikativ.io now resolves to a parked/spam site (AOG777 casino) rather than the project's official site — the official web presence appears gone or compromised.

angles: Self-hosted shared memory as the missing substrate for human+agent collaboration — one versioned, queryable store instead of siloed chat/wiki/ledger/repo tools.
Fork-and-review governance (proposals) as the key trust mechanism that lets you safely give agents write access — a differentiator vs memory-layer tools.
Time travel and as-of reads: history-preserving memory means agents and humans can audit exactly how a page or ledger got to where it is.
Local-first architecture: real Datahike replica in the browser, server as auth boundary not query API — privacy and offline-friendly.
The replikativ stack as a coherent alternative to mainstream agent stacks (Clojure/Datalog/CRDT lineage).
Honest 'known gaps' section as a trust signal for an early-stage tool — and a caution for production use (soft sandbox, blob auth gap, single-node).
replikativ.io being a parked spam site — a red flag for discoverability/credibility that a reviewer should call out.
